private.name: SambaNova Systems
private.rationale: Same sector (Chips & Semiconductors), same stage (Series A), post-money $11B

data.narrative:
Looking Glass, a Series A semiconductor company founded by Shawn Frayne, sits within a comp universe of 11 private peers and 3 public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) in the Chips & Semiconductors sector. The company has raised $30M to date.

The valuation analysis applies one applicable method: Stage-Progression. Using total capital raised ($30M) as a proxy for post-money valuation, a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A progression yields an implied post-money valuation of $60M. Peer-Median triangulation was not applicable; while 11 same-sector peers exist—including SambaNova Systems, Cerebras, PsiQuantum, Etched, and Tenstorrent—the narrow filters for same-stage, adjacent-stage, and similar-valuation-tier comparables yielded insufficient datapoints (fewer than 3), making sector-wide median analysis unreliable.

The single-method triangulation supports a valuation range of $51M (low) to $69M (high), with a median of $60M. This range reflects typical step-up dynamics at the Series A stage but carries material uncertainty due to the sparsity of tightly comparable private peers at similar stages and valuations. Refinement of this range would require either closer visibility into same-stage peer valuations within semiconductor hardware or additional round data for existing comparables.
